name: Meireles
tagline: Beachfront high-rises and the best restaurants
description: Meireles runs along Avenida Beira Mar, a wide palm-lined promenade of jogging paths, coconut stands and a nightly craft market. Behind it sit 20-storey condo towers, banks, pharmacies and the city's densest cluster of good restaurants. It is where most visiting professionals, wealthier locals and long-stay foreigners end up living.
bestFor: Nomads who want to walk out of a serviced apartment onto a safe seafront promenade without ever needing a car.
pros: Walk to the beach, gyms and dozens of restaurants
Best supply of furnished monthly apartments
Well lit and patrolled after dark by Fortaleza standards
cons: Priciest rents in the city, often double inland districts
Beach water quality here is poor, locals swim further east
Constant construction noise from new towers

name: Praia de Iracema
tagline: Bohemian nightlife strip on the old waterfront
description: Iracema is the older, scruffier beach quarter west of Meireles, built around the Ponte dos Ingleses pier and the Dragao do Mar culture centre. Its low colonial buildings hold live forro bars, hostels and galleries, and the streets fill with music on weekend nights. Backpackers, artists and short-stay nomads dominate the rental stock.
bestFor: Sociable nomads who want bars, hostels and live music within stumbling distance.
pros: Cheapest beachfront rents in the tourist zone
Dragao do Mar cultural centre and gallery scene on the doorstep
Dense hostel and coworking cluster makes meeting people easy
cons: Loud until 3am on Friday and Saturday
Noticeably rougher after dark, avoid quiet side streets alone
Visible sex tourism scene puts some people off

name: Aldeota
tagline: The city's professional and shopping core
description: Aldeota is the leafy, moneyed grid one block inland from the beach, full of doctors' offices, private schools, embassies and the Iguatemi shopping mall. Streets are wide with mature trees and gated apartment blocks with pools and gyms. It skews to Brazilian professionals and families rather than tourists.
bestFor: Longer stays where you want a proper apartment, a supermarket and a gym rather than a beach view.
pros: Excellent private clinics, banks and supermarkets
Quieter and safer feeling than the beachfront
Ten minute walk or short ride to Meireles beach
cons: Heavy car traffic and few pedestrian-friendly crossings
Little street life at night, most venues are inside malls
Rents nearly match Meireles without the sea view

name: Coco
tagline: Quiet green district beside the big city park
description: Coco wraps around Parque do Coco, a large mangrove park with running trails and a lake. It is a calm mix of newer condo towers, offices and the Shopping RioMar mall, with far less street noise than the coast. Families and remote workers who want space and greenery over nightlife base here.
bestFor: Remote workers who need silence for calls and a park to run in every morning.
pros: Large park with trails right there
Newer buildings with reliable fibre internet
Better value per square metre than the beach districts
cons: You need a ride or bike to reach the beach
Very little walkable street life outside the malls
Mosquitoes near the mangrove at dusk

name: Benfica
tagline: Student quarter around the federal university
description: Benfica surrounds the Universidade Federal do Ceara campus, giving it cheap lunch counters, photocopy shops, secondhand bookstores and student bars that spill onto the pavement. Housing is older low-rise apartments and shared flats at a fraction of coastal prices. The crowd is young, Brazilian and almost entirely local.
bestFor: Budget nomads and Portuguese learners who want daily contact with locals instead of tourists.
pros: Rents often half what Meireles charges
Cheap set lunches around $4 and lively student bars
Real immersion, very few foreigners around
cons: About 15 minutes by car from the beach
Petty theft is common around the campus edges at night
Older buildings, patchy internet and no lifts in many blocks
